headline: October worst month since war began
dek: Iran is using bomb-laden undersea drones, rocket-propelled grenades and limpet-mine crews against vessels shuttling oil out of the Gulf, in an asymmetric campaign to re-establish fear among shippers; the US runs near-daily escort operations and says the waterway is cleared of Iranian mines…
sources: Wall Street Journal, 'Iran Turns to Guerrilla Tactics in Bid to Reassert Grip on Strait of Hormuz', citing regional officials, security firms and analysts; UKMTO incident counts; Kpler flow data
fault_line: Is Iran's guerrilla campaign winning the shadow war in Hormuz, or is the US escort holding the strait open?

sections.what_happened: Iran is using bomb-laden undersea drones, rocket-propelled grenades and limpet-mine crews against vessels shuttling oil out of the Gulf, in an asymmetric campaign to re-establish fear among shippers; the US runs near-daily escort operations and says the waterway is cleared of Iranian mines (CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper, after a flight over the strait last week). October logged more than 35 Hormuz incidents (UKMTO, Royal Navy-affiliated), the highest monthly number since the war began; at least five vessels struck so far in November. Kpler: oil flows through the strait incl. ship-to-ship transfers averaged ~7.8 million barrels/day in the week through November (preliminary, subject to upward revision), after recently returning to prewar levels; the recovery is now faltering. Brent traded ~$102/barrel Tuesday, US average gasoline ~$4.15/gallon. Monday's US strikes on Qeshm Island were part of unannounced small-scale strikes aimed at halting Iranian attacks on US assets and passing ships.
sections.what_verified: WSJ synthesis; incident counts attributed to UKMTO (T1) and flows to Kpler (T3); the Qeshm-strike and Trump-confirmation elements were independently reported Nov 3-4 by Reuters, AP, AJ and Dawn (see 1100/1200 records). The guerrilla-tactics characterisation itself is WSJ analysis, not an official claim.
sections.what_disputed: US/CENTCOM position (in the same piece) is that the strait is cleared of mines and flows had returned to prewar levels — directly contesting the Iranian campaign's effectiveness; Kpler flow figures are explicitly preliminary. PortWatch note: NO new snapshot — latest remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, observation date 2026-10-18 (STALE flag true): 4 Hormuz transits counted that day, 7-day average 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day. The stale PortWatch count must NOT be presented as current and must NOT be set against the WSJ/Kpler November figures as a like-for-like comparison.
sections.why_matters: Hormuz by the Numbers: 35+ attacks in October, 5+ vessels hit in November — the shadow war in one chart. Proven-set lane (Iran/Gulf shipping war) with hard counted numbers; lead candidate for the next Short.
